title: Knack: pro-Russian group NoName057(16) puts Belgian DDoS researcher on dark-web 'blacklist' seeking information
date_note: Knack reported it on Monday 23 November, according to Belga as published by DH; the list has been visible 'for a few weeks', with no exact posting date given. Knack's own page could not be read.
geo_basis: Only the country is stated (a Belgian researcher); pinned at Brussels as the capital
summary: Belgian magazine Knack reported, as relayed by Belga, that NoName057(16) placed an unnamed Belgian cybersecurity researcher specialising in DDoS protection on a dark-web list of 'citizens hostile to Russia', alongside the president of Eurojust and senior police officials. According to the report, the group offers to pay for more information on those listed and their relatives. Belgium's federal prosecutor confirmed it is running about ten investigations into the group.
plain: A Belgian security researcher who studies a pro-Russian hacker group has been put on that group's online list of people it wants information about, a Belgian magazine reported.
exec: A pro-Russian hacker group reportedly offers to pay for information on people it lists as hostile to Russia, including a Belgian DDoS researcher and senior officials.
impact: One Belgian researcher and senior European officials named on a list seeking information, according to Knack as relayed by Belga; no attack on systems reported.

evidence.quote: Le groupe de hacktivistes pro-russes NoName057(16) a inscrit un Belge sur sa liste noire du dark web
Le parquet fédéral a confirmé qu'il mène une dizaine d'enquêtes.

key_findings: Knack reports NoName057(16) put a Belgian DDoS-protection researcher on a dark-web list of 'citizens hostile to Russia'
The list also names the president of Eurojust, the director of Europol's European Cybercrime Centre and the director general of the German federal police
The group says it will pay for more information on listed people and their relatives
Belgium's federal prosecutor confirmed about ten investigations into the group

validation.note: Only DH (Belga dispatch relaying Knack) was read in full. 7sur7's version and knack.be answered 403, so Knack's original was not checked. The researcher and his company are not named.
